ai.description: *Cnemaspis anaikattiensis* is a small gecko (SVL ~35 mm) with a brownish-grey body, dark-spotted dorsum, and a yellow-tipped tail. It features distinct keeled scales and a prominent precloacal pore.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis anaikattiensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous series of precloacal pores in males, which are absent in most similar species.
ai.habitat: *Cnemaspis anaikattiensis* inhabits rocky outcrops and boulders within moist deciduous forests in the Anaikatti hills of the Western Ghats at elevations around 600–800 meters.
ai.behavior: *Cnemaspis anaikattiensis* is a diurnal gecko that primarily forages on rock surfaces, actively hunting small insects during the day to sustain its energy needs.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis anaikattiensis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, peaking during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis anaikattiensis* is endemic to the Anaikatti Hills in the Western Ghats, spanning the border of Tamil Nadu and Kerala at moderate elevations.
